rows.Origin:
Bred by Tim Hermann Kordes (Germany, 2003).
Introduced in Germany by W. Kordes' Söhne (Retail) in 2012 as 'Kordes' Jubilee'.
rows.Bloom: Yellow, pink edges. Mild, apricot or peach fragrance. 100 to 110 petals. Average diameter 5". Very large, very double, globular, old-fashioned bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Rounded buds.
rows.Habit:
Bushy. Semi-glossy, medium green, leathery foliage. 5 leaflets.

Height: 47" to 4¼' (120 to 130cm). Width: 2' to 28" (60 to 70cm).
rows.Patents:
United States - Patent No: PP 25,530 on 12 May 2015 VIEW USPTO PATENT
Application No: 13/987,687 on 20 Aug 2013
The new variety of rose plant of the present invention originated from a controlled crossing in a breeding program of two distinct parents during the summer of 2003. The crossing was between an ‘un-named seedling’, the seed parent, and another ‘un-named seedling’, the pollen parent by the same inventor.
rows.Notes: Commemorating the 125th anniversary of Kordes & Sons.
